reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Meaning of aircraft in sections 305.010 to 305.110
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 15106; prior revision 1929 § 13905). Defines "aircraft" for sections 305.010 to 305.110 to include balloons, airplanes, hydroplanes, and every other vehicle used for air navigation.

headings.title: Water and air rules for hydroplanes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 15106). Applies water-navigation rules to hydroplanes at rest on water or operated on or immediately above water, and treats them as aircraft when operated through the air otherwise than immediately above water.

headings.title: Meaning of aeronaut
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 15106). Defines "aeronaut" to include aviators, pilots, balloonists, and any other person having any part in operating aircraft while in flight.

headings.title: Meaning of passenger
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 15106). Defines "passenger" to include any person riding in aircraft who has no part in its operation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and RSMo 1939 § 15106 / 1929 § 13905 notes and verified all fingerprints. Checked §§ 305.010–305.110 scope of 'aircraft' and hydroplane water-vs-air distinction; retained all 4 drafted titles.

headings.title: Property acquisition by purchase or condemnation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 15125, A.L. 1943 p. 326; prior revision 1929 § 13924; 2000 City of Bridgeton v. City of St. Louis annotation). Authorizes counties, cities, and special-charter cities to acquire property for an airport, landing field, or addition by purchase or, if unable to agree with owners, by public-purpose or railroad condemnation law.

headings.title: Scope of property subject to acquisition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Broadly defines "property" for this section to include private or public real and personal property, easements or uses, special-district, railroad, and corporate property, churches, graveyards, parks, utilities, and state roads under Highways and Transportation Commission jurisdiction.

headings.title: Bonds, revenue bonds, and airport-location restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes, including the 2000 City of Bridgeton v. City of St. Louis annotation (18 S.W.3d 107) stating that adding runways or expanding existing airport facilities is not deemed establishing a new airport or landing field. Covers voter-approved general bonds, governing-body revenue bonds, and the proviso barring establishment or location violating planning-commission airport plans or zoning regulations. Independent review revised title from 'planning restrictions' to 'airport-location restrictions' so it encompasses both planning-commission airport plans and zoning regulations restricting airport location while preserving the 2000 City of Bridgeton v. City of St. Louis annotation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections, RSMo 1939 § 15125 / 1943 notes, and the 2000 City of Bridgeton v. City of St. Louis (18 S.W.3d 107) annotation, and verified all fingerprints. Revised subsection 3 title to 'Bonds, revenue bonds, and airport-location restrictions' so both planning-commission plans and zoning location restrictions are covered without overstating beyond Bridgeton; retained titles 1–2.

headings.title: State aeronautics program and financial assistance grants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1945 p. 1315 § 1 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 2141 merged with S.B. 818; dual effective dates 8-28-14 for S.B. 818 and 1-01-16 for H.B. 2141; cross-reference to § 155.090 aviation trust fund). Directs the State Highways and Transportation Commission to administer an aeronautics program and authorizes appropriated grants to political subdivisions, state instrumentalities, or FAA-designated privately owned reliever airport owners.

headings.title: Airport control agreements for nonmaintenance state funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Requires recipients of state funds for airport purchase, construction, or improvement—excluding maintenance—to agree before payment to control the airport by ownership or lease for the commission-determined useful life after the last state or federal payment, with the creating governing body assuming the obligation if an airport authority ceases to exist.

headings.title: Aviation trust fund grants, priority, and status
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (including § 155.090 cross-reference). Directs grants from the aviation trust fund unless otherwise provided, requires considering past local support and prioritizing five-year sustained local funding, designates the revolving trust fund exempt from § 33.080 general-revenue transfers, and credits interest to the fund.

headings.title: Aviation trust fund uses, matching ratios, and caps
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4, including subdivisions (1)(a)–(m) and (2)–(4), and source notes (noting dual 2014/2016 effective dates). Details commission administration of appropriated aviation trust fund moneys: up to 90/10 state/local or 50/50 federal-match grants including conditional commercial air-service promotion ($4.5M deposit trigger, $2M cap, $4M non-promotion floor), 100% state safety/charts/education uses, up to $500k/yr ($167k/tower cap) non-federally funded tower operations, and up to $500k/yr ($100k/tower cap) 50/50 nonfederal match for federally cost-shared towers. Independent review revised title to name the aviation trust fund explicitly and capture the conditional commercial air-service promotion trigger/caps in (1)(m) and annual/per-tower control-tower funding caps in (3)–(4).

headings.title: Disaster repair funding and emergency procurement waiver
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes. Allows immediate availability of appropriated airport capital-improvement or maintenance funds upon commission approval after a natural or manmade disaster closes a runway or disables an electronic or visual landing aid, and waives normal engineering and construction procurement requirements for commission-designated emergency projects. Independent review revised title from 'Immediate disaster repair funds' to avoid implying unconditional immediate release independent of commission approval and emergency designation.

headings.title: Meaning of instrumentality of the state
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes. Defines "instrumentality of the state" for this section as a state educational institution under § 176.010 or a state agency that owned or operated an airport on January 1, 1997 and continues to own or operate it.

Revised subsection 4 title to capture aviation trust fund identity and statutory caps/triggers, and subsection 5 title to avoid implying unconditional immediate disaster release; retained titles 1–3 and 6.

headings.title: Technical advice, federal compatibility, and state plan
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1971 S.B. 351; footnote noting word "or" does not appear in original rolls at both bracketed/starred locations). Authorizes free Department of Transportation technical advice to cities, towns, or counties on public airports, mandates technical representation, promotion, planning, and engineering advice for federal program compatibility, and requires developing and maintaining a state airport plan.

headings.title: Approved airport design standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1971 S.B. 351). Directs the department to develop and maintain an "approved airport design" using standard design criteria for airport-user safety and effective use of state and local funds.

headings.title: Local agency designation and governing terms

Authorizes political subdivision governing bodies to designate the department as agent and enter agreements setting agency terms in accordance with federal laws and regulations and sections 305.170 to 305.270.

headings.title: Retention and disbursement of federal grant moneys
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1989 S.B. 448 § 2). Provides that United States grant moneys are retained by the state or paid over to political subdivisions under terms and conditions imposed by the federal government.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and L. 1989 S.B. 448 § 2 history and verified all fingerprints. Verified political-subdivision request prerequisite, §§ 305.170–305.270 cross-reference, and federal grant conditions; retained all 3 titles.

headings.title: Authority approval for local government airport conveyances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Prohibits cities, towns, counties, or political subdivisions within authority boundaries that own an airport from selling, franchising, leasing, contracting operation or maintenance, or conveying it to or with another state, authority, or political subdivision without prior county airport authority approval.

headings.title: Competitive bidding procedures and small-purchase exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires competitive bids for authority purchases, rentals, and leases after newspaper advertisement at least five days before opening, award to lowest and best bidders, right to reject and readvertise, and an exception for estimated expenditures under $1,000.

headings.title: Prohibition on rules conflicting with federal or state law

headings.title: Tax election submission, ballot form, and vote outcome

headings.title: Permitted uses of tax levy revenues

headings.title: Section 70.220 annexation agreements and zoning enforcement remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. headings.title: Local zoning enforcement and authority technical support
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes. Assigns enforcement of adopted §§ 305.500–305.585 airport zoning regulations to city or county zoning/building agencies and requires the authority to supply maps, charts, visual displays, and requested technical advice and representation.

headings.title: Zoning variance standards, conditions, and hazard marking
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and source notes. Requires variance applications for nonconforming structures or natural growth, sets practical-difficulty/unnecessary-hardship and public-interest standards subject to reasonable board conditions, and requires applicant-funded markers, lights, and shielding for resulting hazards. Independent review confirmed variance standards, hazard-marking cost allocation, and verbatim source reference to 'airport zoning board' (distinct from 'committee' in subsection 4).

headings.title: Judicial review of authority zoning decisions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and source notes. Permits aggrieved persons, firms, corporations, or political subdivisions to appeal authority zoning decisions to county circuit court within 30 days after the regulation takes effect, reviewed like other administrative decisions. Independent review confirmed 30-day circuit-court judicial review and retained verbatim source phrasing 'zoning regulations applies'.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties for statutory or zoning violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and source notes. Makes violating §§ 305.500–305.585 or acting contrary to adopted zoning regulations a misdemeanor punished as provided by law, with each day of a zoning violation a separate offense.

headings.title: Compensation under chapter 523 for limiting existing uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and source notes. Prohibits zoning regulations from limiting any existing use without owner consent or compensation for resulting damages or loss in the manner prescribed by chapter 523 (overlapping subsection 2, which also mentions structure height reductions without citing chapter 523).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 11 subsections, history, 2-04-72 effective date, and original-rolls footnote ('Word "to" appears here in original rolls' in subsection 4), and verified all fingerprints. Verified overlap and distinction between subsection 2 (existing uses and structure heights, no chapter 523 citation) and subsection 11 (existing uses with chapter 523 procedure), plus verbatim 'airport zoning board' in (8) and 'zoning regulations applies' in (9); retained all 11 titles.

headings.title: Noise-compatibility findings and major airport zoning area
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1972 H.B. 1341 § 17; effective 2-04-72). States major-airport noise and development findings and authorizes noise-compatibility land-use zoning—in addition to § 305.575—within rectangles extending seven miles from each runway end and one and one-half miles from each side of proposed or planned runway centerlines. Independent review revised title to replace redundant 'zoning zone' with 'zoning area' covering the 7-mile by 1.5-mile runway rectangles.

headings.title: Protection of existing uses and chapter 523 compensation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Prohibits noise-zoning regulations from limiting any existing use without owner consent or compensation for resulting damages or loss in the manner prescribed by chapter 523.

headings.title: Aircraft noise zone establishment, updates, and land-use restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Requires determining probable noise levels and establishing aircraft noise zones within 120 days of new major-airport site approval, permits updates as technology changes, and prohibits land uses or building construction/improvements exposing occupants above acceptable noise levels.

headings.title: Public purpose, property acquisition, and disposition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes. Declares controlling and establishing compatible land use a public purpose for expending funds and acquiring land or property rights, and permits retaining acquired property for lawful use or selling or disposing of it.

headings.title: Major airport land use zoning committee membership and duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes. Directs the chairman to establish a five-member committee—three authority members (one representing the airport county) and two county-resident citizens serving two-year terms—to recommend zoning regulations and hear land-use zoning appeals.

headings.title: Adoption, notice, and appeal procedures under section 305.575
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes. Applies § 305.575 adoption, change, notice, and judicial-appeal procedures to noise-zoning regulations and authority decisions under this section.

headings.title: Noise-zoning variance standards, conditions, and soundproofing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes. Requires variance applications for nonconforming structures or uses, sets hardship/public-interest standards subject to reasonable board conditions, and mandates applicant-funded soundproofing, lights, and protection against aircraft noise. Independent review confirmed variance standards, applicant-funded soundproofing, and verbatim source phrasing 'noncompliance use' and 'airport land use zoning board'.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 7 subsections, history, and 2-04-72 effective date, and verified all fingerprints. Checked § 305.575 and chapter 523 cross-references, 120-day noise-zone timeline, and verbatim 'noncompliance use'/'airport land use zoning board' in (7); revised subsection 1 title to replace redundant 'zoning zone' with 'zoning area'; retained titles 2–7.

headings.title: Short title of Airport Relocation Assistance Act
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1510 § 1; effective 6-14-90). Designates sections 305.600 to 305.630 as the "Airport Relocation Assistance Act".

headings.title: Compliance with federal uniform relocation regulations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Requires displacing agencies, except as otherwise provided in sections 305.600 to 305.630, to comply with federal Department of Transportation regulations under the Federal Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970, as amended.

headings.title: Meaning of displacing agencies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Defines "displacing agencies" for sections 305.600 to 305.630 as state, local, and private entities using eminent domain to relocate persons for constructing or expanding airports located in a first-class charter county and operated by a city not within a county.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections, history, and 6-14-90 effective date, and verified all fingerprints. Checked short title, qualified federal uniform relocation compliance, and first-class charter county / city-not-within-a-county scope of 'displacing agencies'; retained all 3 titles.

headings.title: Moving, personal-property loss, search, and reestablishment payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1)–(4), and source notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1510 § 2; effective 6-14-90). Requires displacing-agency heads to pay displaced residential or business persons—in addition to real-estate compensation—actual reasonable moving expenses, capped direct tangible personal-property losses from moving or discontinuing a business/farm, replacement search expenses, and up to $10,000 in farm, nonprofit, or small-business reestablishment expenses.

headings.title: Optional federal-schedule expense and dislocation allowance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Allows persons eligible under subsection 1 to elect an expense and dislocation allowance determined under U.S. Department of Transportation criteria and schedule in lieu of subsection 1 payments.

headings.title: Discretionary extraordinary relocation payments to utility facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Authorizes displacing agencies to provide additional relocation payments to utility facilities incurring extraordinary relocation costs as determined under federal law and DOT regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections (including 1(1)–(4)), history, and 6-14-90 effective date, and verified all fingerprints. Verified $10,000 reestablishment cap, optional U.S. DOT schedule election, and permissive ('may') extraordinary utility relocation payments; retained all 3 titles.

headings.title: Homeowner replacement-housing, interest, and closing-cost payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1)–(3), and source notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1510 § 3; effective 6-14-90). Mandates an additional payment up to $22,500 for displaced homeowners owning and occupying a dwelling at least 180 days before negotiations, covering comparable replacement cost differential, increased mortgage interest/debt-service costs on 180-day bona fide mortgages, and non-prepaid title, recording, and closing costs.

headings.title: One-year replacement purchase deadline and good-cause extensions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (including footnote noting word "this" appears in original rolls where text prints "the" before "date"). Conditions payment on purchasing and occupying a decent, safe, and sanitary replacement dwelling within one year after final payment or satisfaction of § 305.609 obligations (whichever is later), with good-cause extensions capped at one-year relocation costs.

headings.title: State agency insurance of replacement-dwelling mortgages
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Authorizes state agency heads, upon mortgagee application, to insure replacement-dwelling mortgages (including construction advances) and issue pre-execution commitments notwithstanding statutory age, physical-condition, or personal-characteristic mortgagor requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections (including 1(1)–(3)), history, 6-14-90 effective date, and original-rolls footnote ('Word "this" appears in original rolls' at 'the* date' in subsection 2), and verified all fingerprints. Checked 180-day occupancy/mortgage rules, $22,500 cap, § 305.609 trigger, and state mortgage insurance; retained all 3 titles.

headings.title: Rental assistance payments for ninety-day dwelling occupants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) and (2), and source notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1510 § 4; effective 6-14-90). Requires displacing agencies to pay up to $5,250 for up to 42 months' comparable replacement rent for § 305.606-ineligible displaced persons who lawfully occupied a dwelling at least 90 days before negotiations or a U.S. DOT-prescribed non-acquisition event, with discretionary installments and income consideration for low-income persons.

headings.title: Election to apply rental payment toward dwelling purchase
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Allows subsection 1-eligible persons to apply payments toward a down payment and incidental purchase costs for a decent, safe, and sanitary replacement dwelling up to the discretionary subsection 1 maximum, subject to a § 305.606 cap for 90-to-180-day displaced homeowners.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections (including 1(1)–(2)), history, and 6-14-90 effective date, and verified all fingerprints. Checked 90-day occupancy, 42-month/$5,250 limits, low-income computation rule, and 90-to-180-day homeowner § 305.606 cap; retained both titles.

headings.title: Early project planning to minimize displacement impacts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) and (2), and source notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1510 § 5; effective 6-14-90). Requires displacing agencies to plan programs or projects early to recognize displacement problems for individuals, families, businesses, and farms and provide for their resolution to minimize adverse impacts and expedite completion. Independent review confirmed early planning mandate and retained verbatim source phrasing 'adverse impacts in displaced persons'.

headings.title: Availability of advisory services to displaced and adjacent persons
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Requires making subsection 3 advisory services available to all displaced persons and permits making them available to adjacent-property occupants (retaining verbatim archived source text "has caused substantial economic injury" without editorial repair).

headings.title: Required elements of relocation advisory programs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, including subdivisions (1)–(3), and source notes. Requires advisory programs to determine needs and preferences, furnish current comparable replacement housing and business/farm location availability and pricing data, and assure no move from a dwelling without reasonable opportunity to relocate to a comparable replacement dwelling.

headings.title: Coordination with federal, state, and local governmental actions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes. Directs displacing-agency heads to coordinate relocation activities with other federal, state, or local governmental actions affecting delivery of relocation assistance.

headings.title: Discretionary advisory services for short-term post-acquisition tenants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes. Makes short-term or terminable rental occupants of property acquired by a displacing agency eligible for advisory services to the extent determined by the agency.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections (including 1(1)–(2) and 3(1)–(3)), history, and 6-14-90 effective date, and verified all fingerprints. Verified verbatim source quirks ('adverse impacts in displaced persons' in 1(2) and 'has caused substantial economic injury' in 2) retained without editorial repair, plus discretionary short-term tenant scope in (5); retained all 5 titles.

headings.title: Providing unavailable replacement dwellings and exceeding caps
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1510 § 6; effective 6-14-90; footnote noting word "to" appears in original rolls where text prints "or" in "necessary or appropriate"). Authorizes displacing-agency heads, when comparable replacement dwellings are unavailable and delaying a project, to use project funds to provide dwellings and exceed § 305.606 payment caps case by case for good cause under lead-agency regulations. Independent review revised title to remove non-statutory 'Last-resort' terminology while covering project-funded dwelling provision, good-cause case-by-case § 305.606 cap exceptions, and the original-rolls 'to' footnote.

headings.title: Comparable housing prerequisite for federally assisted moves
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Prohibits requiring any person to move from a dwelling due to a federal or federally assisted program or project unless the displacing-agency head is satisfied comparable replacement housing is available.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections, history, 6-14-90 effective date, and original-rolls footnote ('Word "to" appears in original rolls' at 'necessary or* appropriate' in subsection 1), and verified all fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 title to 'Providing unavailable replacement dwellings and exceeding caps' to avoid non-statutory 'last-resort' jargon; retained title 2.

headings.title: Ninety-day deadline for clearing acquired residential property
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1510 § 10; effective 6-14-90). Requires a displacing agency to clear acquired residential relocation property as soon as possible and within 90 days after physical possession and utility disconnection notification.

headings.title: Grading, seeding, and mowing of acquired property
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Requires the displacing agency to grade acquired property and keep it in good condition by seeding and mowing.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections, history, and 6-14-90 effective date, and verified all fingerprints. Checked 90-day clearing trigger (physical possession plus utility disconnection notice) and grading/seeding/mowing duty; retained both titles.

headings.title: High-noise property buyouts and neighborhood noise monitors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1510 § 11, A.L. 1993 H.B. 710). Requires purchasing areas surrounding an expanding § 305.600 airport rated 75 LDN or greater within a reasonable time, placing and maintaining surrounding noise monitors, and installing/maintaining monitors in neighborhoods within three miles upon request of at least 10% of residents.

headings.title: Perimeter buffer zone, buyouts, exemptions, and landscaping
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires planning a 1,000-foot perimeter zone when property is acquired for airport use, permits exempting areas under 65 LDN, requires purchasing residences upon majority property-owner agreement without barring voluntary buyouts or non-noise purchase requests, and requires landscaping the buffer as a visual barrier.

headings.title: Relocation of neighborhood access roads and state highways
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires relocating rather than eliminating neighborhood access roads affected by airport expansion, and relocating affected state-maintained or regulated highways under transportation-department supervision at airport expense, with optional department cost-sharing for highway expansion.

headings.title: Demolition, debris clearing, and restoration of noise-mitigation land
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires demolishing unused structures, clearing debris, and allowing noise-mitigation land purchased in an airport expansion to return to its natural condition within six months after vacating.

headings.title: Floodplain review and approval of airport expansion plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires filing proposed airport expansion plans with the Department of Natural Resources and directs approval if the plan will not adversely affect nearby floodplains so as to cause significant floodwater damage risk. Independent review revised title for conciseness and neutral sentence casing while retaining DNR floodplain filing and approval criteria.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections and 1990/1993 history and verified all fingerprints. Checked § 305.600 75-LDN buyouts, 3-mile/10% neighborhood monitor requests, 1,000-foot perimeter zone and <65-LDN exemption, road/highway relocation, 6-month restoration, and DNR floodplain review; revised subsection 5 title to 'Floodplain review and approval of airport expansion plans'; retained titles 1–4.

headings.title: Discovery record and ownership or lienholder inquiry
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1)–(2)(b), and history note (L. 2020 H.B. 1963). Requires an airport superintendent discovering a derelict or abandoned aircraft to record the discovery date and inquire into owners and lienholders via FAA aircraft registration records or an aircraft title search company.

headings.title: Certified-mail notice contents and ten-business-day deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1)–(6), and history note. Requires certified-mail, return-receipt notice within 10 business days of receiving subsection 1 information covering aircraft location, accrued fees, § 305.806 lien, enforcement, 30-day § 305.804 disposition warning, and faster removal for health or safety dangers. Independent review revised title from 'ten-day' to 'ten-business-day' to preserve the statutory distinction from the 30-calendar-day periods in subdivisions (5)–(6); retained verbatim 'under this section' in (4).

headings.title: Posted weatherproof notice for unknown or unfound owners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, including subdivisions (1) and (2), and history note. Requires conspicuously posting a weatherproof or laminated notice at least 8 by 10 inches containing subsection 2(2)–(6) information on the aircraft if the owner is unknown or cannot be found after subsection 1(2) inquiry. Independent review revised title to cover both unknown owners and owners who cannot be found after subsection 1(2) inquiry.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections (including 1(1)–(2)(b), 2(1)–(6), and 3(1)–(2)) and L. 2020 H.B. 1963 history, and verified all fingerprints. Revised subsection 2 title to specify 'ten-business-day deadline' (distinguishing 30-calendar-day periods in (5)–(6)) and subsection 3 title to cover both unknown and unfound owners; retained verbatim 'under this section' in 2(4) and title 1.

headings.title: Disposition options after thirty-day notice period
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1)–(4), and history note (L. 2020 H.B. 1963). Authorizes the airport superintendent to retain, trade to another local or state entity, sell, or dispose of through a refuse/salvage company an aircraft if the owner or interested party fails to remove it, pay accrued fees and costs in full, or show reasonable cause within 30 calendar days of posting notice under § 305.802. Independent review confirmed all four disposition options, reasonable-cause exception, and verbatim 30-calendar-day trigger tied to 'posting notice under section 305.802'.

headings.title: Public auction and notice requirements for aircraft sales
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires selling aircraft under subsection 1(3) at public auction after at least 10 calendar days' newspaper notice in the airport county and written notice to all known interested parties.

headings.title: Negotiated pricing and recordkeeping for refuse or salvage disposal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes negotiating payment from or to a refuse/salvage company under subsection 1(4) and requires preparing and maintaining price-establishment and justification records.

headings.title: Owner liability for deficiency after sale or disposal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Holds the aircraft owner liable for remaining unpaid fees and charges not offset by a lower sale or negotiated disposal price.

headings.title: Owner liability for removal, storage, and sale costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Makes all removal, storage, and sale costs incurred by the airport superintendent recoverable against the aircraft owner.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections (including 1(1)–(4)) and L. 2020 H.B. 1963 history, and verified all fingerprints. Verified 30-calendar-day notice/reasonable-cause trigger (retaining verbatim 'posting notice under section 305.802'), 10-calendar-day auction notice, negotiated salvage records, and owner deficiency/cost liability; retained all 5 titles.

headings.title: Lien scope and prerequisite notice to interested parties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2020 H.B. 1963). Grants the airport superintendent a lien on a derelict or abandoned aircraft for unpaid airport fees/charges and transportation, storage, and removal costs, conditioned on serving prerequisite notice on the last registered owner and legal or equitable interest holders.

headings.title: Claim-of-lien contents, verification, service, and section 400.9-501 filing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1)–(4), and history note. Specifies required claim-of-lien contents, sworn execution by the director or designee, pre-filing service on the owner and interest holders, and filing under § 400.9-501 as constructive notice establishing lien attachment and priority.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections (including 2(1)–(4)) and L. 2020 H.B. 1963 history, and verified all fingerprints. Checked prerequisite notice, sworn claim-of-lien contents, pre-filing service, and § 400.9-501 filing/priority rules; retained both titles.

headings.title: Satisfaction of lien and sale expenses from proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2020 H.B. 1963). Directs the airport superintendent, if an aircraft is sold, to satisfy the lien plus reasonable notice, advertisement, and sale expenses from the proceeds.

headings.title: Holding and delivering remaining sale proceeds to owner
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires holding any remaining balance of sale proceeds and delivering it on demand to the aircraft owner.

headings.title: Airport retention of unclaimed proceeds after twelve months
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes the airport to retain unclaimed proceeds for airport operations if no person claims the balance within 12 months of the sale date.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and L. 2020 H.B. 1963 history, and verified all fingerprints. Checked sale-proceeds application, demand delivery of balance to owner, and 12-month unclaimed-funds retention for airport operations; retained all 3 titles.

headings.title: Lawful ownership and divestment of prior notified interests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2020 H.B. 1963). Confers lawful ownership on a person acquiring a legal interest under §§ 305.800–305.810 and divests other legal or equitable interests, provided their holders were notified of intended disposal as required under §§ 305.800–305.810.

headings.title: Issuance of disposition documents to purchasers or recipients
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes the airport superintendent to issue documents of disposition to purchasers or recipients of aircraft disposed of under §§ 305.800–305.810.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and L. 2020 H.B. 1963 history, and verified all fingerprints. Verified notice proviso conditioning divestment of prior legal or equitable interests and permissive issuance of disposition documents; retained both titles.
